action_trace.summary: Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals, pain points, and acceptance criteria for ES|QL multi-valued field aggregation semantics and unbounded SORT + MV_EXPAND error messaging improvements. Questions probe user expectations for null handling in array values, error clarity, workflow context, and prioritization to inform requirements refinement.

Generated 10 interview questions targeting user goals (aggregation intent, workflow context), pain points (error clarity, unexpected null semantics, workaround burden), and acceptance criteria (error message specificity, behavioral predictability) using 5W1H and Socratic techniques grounded in the elasticsearch_2026q1 multi-value aggregation and unbounded SORT requirements.

Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (achieving successful SORT+MV_EXPAND queries), pain points (unclear error messaging, diagnostic difficulty), and acceptance criteria (actionable error messages with command-specific guidance and remediation examples). Questions decompose the requirement into user impact, workflow context, and success metrics aligned with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 stakeholder analysis.

End users need clearer ES|QL error messages for SORT+MV_EXPAND conflicts and explicit documentation of multi-value field behavior in expressions to reduce debugging time and prevent silent data loss in aggregations.

End users require explicit, actionable error messages for SORT+MV_EXPAND conflicts and transparent, documented rules for multi-value field expression evaluation to prevent silent data loss and reduce debugging friction in ES|QL aggregations.

End-users face two critical gaps in ES|QL: (1) opaque error messaging for SORT/MV_EXPAND conflicts that prevents diagnosis and remediation, and (2) unintuitive multi-value field handling in expressions that silently causes data loss. Expectations center on explicit error context, transparent semantics documentation, and proactive validation warnings to enable confident query construction.

Clarification needed on: (1) scope and cascading effects of null behavior in multi-value field expressions within aggregations, (2) whether LIMIT is the only mitigation or if command reordering is supported for SORT+MV_EXPAND, (3) whether improved error messaging should be command-specific or generic, and (4) whether silent null returns for multi-value arithmetic should trigger user warnings.

EndUser raises 6 clarification questions targeting ambiguities in multi-value field expression semantics (null propagation, aggregation inclusion rules), unbounded SORT error messaging strategy, and scope of error message improvements for ES|QL command interactions.

Three core ambiguities require resolution: (1) whether null behavior for multi-value expressions cascades through aggregation functions or applies only locally, (2) the precise counting semantics for SUM(X+4) when X has multiple values, and (3) whether the improved error message should recommend LIMIT, command reordering, or both as equally valid mitigations for unbounded SORT before MV_EXPAND.

End-user confirms multi-value field null behavior is expression-level with aggregation propagation; refines error message requirement to explicitly identify problematic command sequence and provide both LIMIT and MV_EXPAND reordering as valid mitigations; emphasizes need for deterministic, documented behavior to prevent silent data loss in aggregations.

End-user requirements validated and refined: (1) Multi-value field expressions null behavior confirmed to propagate through aggregations; (2) STATS aggregation logic clarified with concrete example; (3) Unbounded SORT error messaging must explicitly identify command sequence and present both valid mitigation strategies (LIMIT or reorder); (4) Overall requirement for transparent, non-silent handling of multi-value field semantics in ES|QL to prevent data loss and improve error diagnostics.

End-user confirms multi-value field expression semantics (X+a=null for multi-value X, propagating through aggregations) and refines error messaging for SORT+MV_EXPAND to explicitly state root cause and present both valid mitigation strategies (LIMIT or reordering). Requires transparent documentation and actionable error guidance to prevent silent data loss.

Consolidated 7 structured elicitation records from EndUser dialogue addressing two primary requirement clusters: (1) Multi-value field arithmetic null propagation semantics in aggregations with explicit documentation requirements, and (2) Unbounded SORT before MV_EXPAND error messaging with dual mitigation strategies. All items mapped to ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 requirement format with priority levels and traceability to confirmed user expectations and clarifications.

Six hierarchical user requirements synthesized from elasticsearch_2026q1 case addressing multi-value field arithmetic null propagation (3 MUST), unbounded SORT error messaging and mitigation (2 MUST + 1 SHOULD), and documentation clarity (1 MUST). All requirements prioritized via MoSCoW and traced to validated enduser confirmations and pain points.

Targeted Deployer dialogue probing infrastructure readiness for ES|QL error message improvements: deployment topology support, security constraints on error content, query validation architecture, field metadata availability, tooling synchronization, backward compatibility risks, and rollout strategy—enabling assessment of feasibility for REQ-ES-SORT-001/002/003 and multi-value field null-propagation requirements.

Eight targeted questions probe infrastructure execution constraints (unbounded SORT architectural limits, error context propagation), security implications (SORT ordering and data exposure), scalability thresholds (cardinality density, aggregation cost), and deployment logistics (backward compatibility, validation delivery, documentation versioning) to ground infrastructure and security requirements for ES|QL multi-value field handling and error messaging improvements.

Targeted dialogue questions for Deployer addressing infrastructure constraints (query engine limits, error pipeline architecture), security implications (DOS risks of unbounded results), scalability expectations (multi-value field cardinality, MV_EXPAND performance thresholds), and deployment concerns (backward compatibility, rollout strategy, observability requirements) for ES|QL multi-value field arithmetic and SORT-before-MV_EXPAND improvements.

Deployer confirms infrastructure readiness for ES|QL multi-value field and SORT-MV_EXPAND requirements: 3-node HA cluster with expression validation pipeline, pre-execution error detection, null-propagation caching, secure error messaging, and operational runbooks for LIMIT/SORT-repositioning mitigation strategies. Documentation and monitoring enable end-user self-service troubleshooting.

Deployer confirms infrastructure requirements for 3-node ES|QL cluster with pre-execution SORT-MV_EXPAND validation; security constraints mandate sanitized error messaging; scalability achieved through expression evaluation caching at query compilation; operational procedures specify structured error responses with dual mitigation strategies; documentation and optional warnings address end-user pain points around multi-value field null-propagation and unbounded sort errors.

Deployer confirms infrastructure requirements: 3-node minimum Elasticsearch cluster with ES|QL query engine, pre-execution validation layer for SORT-before-MV_EXPAND detection, and expression evaluation caching at compilation stage. Security mandate: sanitize error messages to prevent information disclosure while maintaining diagnostic clarity (explicitly name problematic commands). Scalability strategy: implement early-exit optimization in aggregation pipeline and O(n) async validation for warnings. Availability requirement: present both mitigation strategies (LIMIT, SORT reordering) equally in error messages to prevent user bias toward suboptimal patterns.

Deployer raises 5 clarification questions on incomplete requirement fragments (null-propagation scope, arithmetic operation coverage, error message command identification, cache timing, and security boundaries for diagnostic information) to establish sufficient operational context before deployment validation.

Deployer identified three incomplete requirement fragments requiring textual completion, two notation inconsistencies requiring semantic clarification, and three infrastructure/security/scalability constraints requiring deployment trade-off confirmation before implementation can proceed.

Deployer raises five critical clarifications: (1) incomplete requirement fragment on SUM(X+4) evaluation logic requires completion, (2) symbolic vs. literal notation ('X+a' vs 'X+4') scope must be defined, (3) error message specification for SORT-MV_EXPAND command naming is incomplete, (4) infrastructure validation needed on query-validation layer timing (parse vs. runtime), and (5) security validation required on error message sanitization constraints. All clarifications block operational deployment until resolved.

Deployer validates infrastructure readiness (3-node cluster, query validation layer for SORT-MV_EXPAND detection), confirms security sanitization of error messages, validates expression evaluation caching strategy for scalability, and resolves incomplete requirement fragments by confirming null-propagation applies uniformly to all derived expressions and error messages must specify both root cause (SORT before MV_EXPAND) and dual mitigation strategies (LIMIT or reorder).

Deployer validates and refines elasticsearch_2026q1 requirements: confirms 3+ node infrastructure with ES|QL SORT-before-MV_EXPAND detection at validation layer, security-compliant error messaging naming both commands with dual mitigation strategies, and query-compilation-stage caching for null-propagation logic to ensure scalability. Resolves incomplete requirement fragments by confirming X+a null-propagation behavior (a=any arithmetic operation), STATS SUM example semantics [18,7], and error message specification. All requirements aligned with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 and availability-cost-performance trade-offs.

Deployer validates infrastructure readiness (3+ node Elasticsearch cluster with ES|QL support), security hardening (sanitized error messages without internal exposure), and scalability (compilation-stage caching for null-propagation). Three incomplete requirement fragments require clarification before final deployment sign-off: SUM(X+4) aggregation boundary, 'X+a' notation standardization, and error message command specification.

Elasticsearch 2026Q1 operating environment requires a 3+ node cluster with ES|QL query engine implementing: (1) expression-level null propagation for multi-value field arithmetic with aggregation function integration; (2) compilation-stage SORT-before-MV_EXPAND detection with explicit, command-specific error messaging offering both LIMIT and reordering mitigations; (3) expression evaluation caching at compilation stage for performance; (4) sanitized error outputs preventing information disclosure; (5) comprehensive documentation and pre-execution validation warnings to address user pain points around null behavior unintuitive handling and generic error messages.

Consolidated 10 system requirements (IEEE 830 format) addressing multi-value field expression null-propagation semantics, SORT-before-MV_EXPAND error detection and messaging, documentation clarity, security sanitization, and infrastructure validation. Requirements integrate user pain points (confusing errors, unintuitive multi-value handling), deployer constraints (3-node cluster, expression caching, security), and confirmed clarifications from enduser confirmations and deployer validations.

SysML Block Definition Diagram with Activity Diagram selected as primary modeling methodology. BDD captures structural decomposition of Elasticsearch|QL query pipeline (Expression Evaluator, Validation Layer, MV_EXPAND/SORT operators) with formal constraint specifications for null-propagation semantics. Activity Diagram models critical query compilation workflow including SORT-before-MV_EXPAND detection and expression evaluation caching. Dual-model approach satisfies IEEE 830/ISO 29148 requirements for precise interface specifications, traceability, and quality attribute allocation. Supplements with UML Sequence Diagram for temporal ordering validation. Rejects Use Case/ER/State Machine diagrams as insufficient for capturing internal system mechanics and expression evaluation formalism.

Requirement model reveals 10 critical gaps and conflicts: incomplete requirement fragments (SORT error message, SUM example), symbolic/literal notation inconsistency (X+a vs X+4), ambiguous mitigation strategy priority, missing edge-case definitions, security sanitization scope ambiguity, validation timing conflict between static/runtime detection, absent performance criteria for expression caching, and missing operational/infrastructure specifications. Chain-of-Thought analysis indicates REQ-ES-MV-001/002 and REQ-ES-SORT-001/002/003 are structurally sound but require clarification of boundary conditions, cache invalidation logic, error message diagnostic scope, and dual-mitigation strategy validation before SysML BDD/Activity Diagram modeling can proceed. Recommend gap closure iteration with stakeholders before formal requirements traceability matrix generation.

Notation inconsistencies standardized, incomplete specifications completed, acceptance criteria and detection metrics defined, and dual mitigation strategies validated. SRS-ES-2026Q1 sections 003-006 now meet ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 quality attributes (clarity, verifiability, consistency, traceability). Ready for development phase.
